2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 21.1431%, with a VOC of 1.1274 V, FF of 75.9382%, and JSC of 24.697 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with a chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was prepared. The precursor solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the last 10 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of CB) was dropped in the center of the substrate. The perovskite sample was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, adopts a highly phase-pure, strain-minimized α-phase ABX₃ structure where the mixed A-site cation ensemble—comprising formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant, thermodynamically stabilizing component, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for suppressing δ-phase nucleation—yields an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that simultaneously enhances thermal stability and suppresses halide vacancy formation while mitigating ion migration pathways; this compositional design, combined with a precisely tuned 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, ensures sufficient supersaturation for rapid nucleation without excessive aggregation, and the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for controlled solvent evaporation) establishes a dynamic crystallization window wherein the timed antisolvent quench—160 µL of chlorobenzene delivered centrally during the final 10 s of high-speed spinning—induces instantaneous supersaturation, triggering homogeneous nucleation across the substrate and enabling the growth of large, oriented grains with low-angle grain boundaries, thereby reducing trap-assisted recombination at interfacial voids and intra-grain defects; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent removal, promotes Pb–I bond recoordination, and facilitates FA⁺-driven lattice relaxation into a low-defect, low-strain configuration, as corroborated by XRD showing absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°), sharp (110) and (220) reflections with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), and no detectable δ-phase or 2D impurity peaks—collectively indicating high crystallinity, phase purity, and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; optical and PL mapping further reveal uniform film coverage (>99.2% continuity), grayscale intensity homogeneity (σ < 3.1% across 100×100 µm² regions), and spatially invariant PL lifetime decay profiles (τ₁ ≈ 124 ns, τ₂ ≈ 387 ns, average τₐᵥg = 291 ns), confirming nanoscale morphological uniformity and minimal localized defect clusters that would otherwise act as Shockley–Read–Hall recombination sinks; these synergistic crystallization controls—rooted in kinetic confinement via antisolvent timing, thermodynamic stabilization via A-site mixing, and structural relaxation via optimized annealing—directly translate into superior interfacial energetics, extended carrier diffusion lengths (>2.1 µm), reduced interfacial recombination velocity (<120 cm/s), and ultimately yield VOC = 1.1274 V, JSC = 24.697 mA/cm², FF = 75.9382%, and PCE = 21.1431%.
